method: Code review through the Lovable MCP, read-only (list_edits, get_diff, read_file, list_files, list_messages). No send_message, deploy, set_*, respond_to_approval or query_database. The preview needs a login, so it was not run. Image findings come from the owner's 1920px screenshot.

regressions: Raw i18n keys on screen. LeadForm.jsx still calls the old leadForm.* keys, but the new locale files use lead_form.*, so every label of the lead form renders as text like 'leadForm.title' or 'leadForm.name *'. CheckoutButton.jsx calls checkout.comingSoon and nav.bookConsultation, which no longer exist. IntlArticles.jsx calls articles.allCategories, which is missing too.

The header nav wraps onto two lines at 1920px. It holds 7 links, the 3-language switcher and the CTA pill, all inside max-w-6xl (1120px of content) from the lg breakpoint up, with no whitespace-nowrap.
IntlPrivacy.jsx reads useParams().slug, but the routes are /:lang/privacy|terms|accessibility and have no :slug param. As a result /terms and /accessibility show the privacy-policy text.
The catch-all '*' route renders the Hebrew PageNotFound ('הדף לא נמצא'), so EN/FR visitors who mistype a URL get a Hebrew 404.

supabase/migrations/20260723223655_ecad6198-…: REVOKE EXECUTE FROM anon, public; GRANT EXECUTE TO authenticated (both functions)
supabase/migrations/20260723232742_bf5a192f-…: ALTER FUNCTION get_rabbi_students_safe(uuid) SECURITY INVOKER; ALTER FUNCTION get_student_safe_data(uuid) SECURITY INVOKER

Conclusion: before 0068 both functions were INVOKER, with no body auth check, anon/PUBLIC revoked and authenticated granted. 0068 keeps exactly that (INVOKER is the default, explicit REVOKE/GRANT, plus an explicit service_role grant that it already had through default privileges). Nothing needed restoring. 'No later redefinition before 0068' is Lovable's claim; I verified the four cited files, not every migration from 0000 to 0067.
deliverables.begin_commit_judgement: Acceptable. 0068 already ran in production, so editing an applied migration would only change its hash and history. Drizzle's migrator runs pending migrations inside its own transaction, so an inner COMMIT would end that transaction early on a fresh run. The rollback file has its own BEGIN/COMMIT. Caveat: this holds only if the deploy runner is drizzle migrate(), not a raw psql -f.
